info.name: WebChannel
info.comment: Exchanges text and binary messages with a remote peer over a PeerConnection.

description.p: A WebChannel is a bidirectional message channel that is carried by a PeerConnection. Messages are always delivered whole, and each is flagged as either text or binary. A connection can carry many channels, each with its own label, ordering and reliability settings.

WebChannel objects cannot be created directly. A local channel is created with PeerConnection.CreateWebChannel(), and a channel that is announced by the remote peer is delivered through PeerConnection.OnWebChannel. In both cases the channel is owned by the PeerConnection and is destroyed with it. The Label, Protocol, Negotiated, Ordered, MaxRetransmits and MaxPacketLifeTime fields are set on creation and cannot be changed.

A new channel starts in the CONNECTING state and calls OnOpen when it is ready for use. A local channel opens once the remote peer acknowledges it, or once the connection is established if the channel is negotiated. A remote channel is reported through PeerConnection.OnWebChannel before any of its other events. Messages are then sent with Send and received through OnMessage.
When a channel closes normally, OnClose is called once. If the channel fails, OnError is called first, followed by OnClose. Freeing a channel closes it without making any further callbacks.

Channel events are delivered by the parent's framework timer, so the thread that created the PeerConnection must process messages, and the channel must only be used from that thread. Callbacks are never made from within a call to Send or Close. A callback can safely send messages, or close or free the channel or its parent.

method.name: Close
method.comment: Closes the channel in both directions.

description.p: Close() changes State to CLOSING and rejects any further calls to Send. Reliable messages that have already been queued are delivered before the channel's stream is reset. Partially reliable messages remain subject to their MaxRetransmits or MaxPacketLifeTime limits. OnClose is called once the remote peer has completed the reset.
If the remote peer does not complete the reset within five seconds, the connection fails with ERR::Timeout. A channel that has not yet been assigned a stream is closed immediately.
Calling Close() on a channel that is closing or closed has no effect. Freeing the channel also closes it, but without calling OnClose.

method.name: Send
method.comment: Queues a message for delivery to the remote peer.
method.prototype: ERR wch::Send(OBJECTPTR Object, std::span<const int8_t> Data, WCM Type)

input.param: Declares the message as TEXT or BINARY.

description.p: Send() copies a complete message to the channel's send queue and returns immediately. The message is either queued in full or rejected, and is delivered to the remote peer as a single message. A successful result does not indicate that the message has been sent or received. The number of bytes awaiting transmission is reported by BufferedAmount.

The Type is delivered with the message so that the receiver can tell text from binary data; the content itself is not altered. Use TEXT for strings, which browsers receive as a JavaScript string, and BINARY for arbitrary bytes, which browsers receive as an ArrayBuffer or Blob. Both types can be mixed on the same channel. Refer to RFC 8831 for further information.
The channel must be in the OPEN state. Messages of type TEXT must be valid UTF-8, and no message can exceed MaxMessageSize. Empty messages are permitted.

The send queue is limited to 16 MiB and 1024 messages for each channel, and 32 MiB and 4096 messages across the connection. If a message would exceed these limits it is rejected with ERR::BufferOverflow, and the client should wait for OnBufferedAmountLow before sending more data. Messages are also rejected with ERR::BufferOverflow while 4094 or more channel events, such as received messages, are awaiting delivery to the client's callbacks.
In Tiri, Data can be a string, which may contain embedded null bytes, an array<byte>, or nil for an empty message.

result.error: A TEXT message is not valid UTF-8.
The remote peer does not support partially reliable delivery.
The send queue is full, or too many channel events are awaiting delivery.
Type is not a recognised value.

field.name: BufferedAmount
field.comment: The number of message bytes that are queued and have not yet been transmitted.

description.p: BufferedAmount counts the message content that has been queued with Send but not yet passed to the transport. It decreases as data is transmitted, or when partially reliable messages are abandoned. Protocol overhead and retransmissions are not counted.

Transmitted data continues to occupy the send queue until the remote peer acknowledges it, so Send can reject a message with ERR::BufferOverflow even when BufferedAmount is low. Use BufferedAmountLowThreshold and OnBufferedAmountLow to regulate the rate of sending.

field.name: BufferedAmountLowThreshold
field.comment: The BufferedAmount level, in bytes, at which OnBufferedAmountLow is called.

description.p: OnBufferedAmountLow is called when BufferedAmount falls from above this threshold to a value at or below it. The default is zero, and the value can be set from 0 to 16777216. Changing the threshold does not trigger a callback.

field.name: Error
field.comment: The error that caused the channel to fail.

description.p: Error is set when the channel fails, before OnError is called. It remains ERR::Okay if the channel opens and closes normally.
Label is a UTF-8 string that is set when the channel is created. For a channel created by the remote peer, it is the label chosen by that peer. Labels do not need to be unique.

field.name: MaxMessageSize
field.comment: The largest message, in bytes, that can be sent to the remote peer.

description.p: MaxMessageSize reflects the limit advertised in the remote peer's session description, and is zero until the remote description has been applied. If the remote peer does not advertise a limit, the default is 65536 bytes. If it advertises no limit, or a limit above 16 MiB, the value is capped at 16 MiB. Messages sent with Send cannot exceed this size.

field.name: MaxPacketLifeTime
field.comment: The maximum lifetime of an outgoing message, in milliseconds.

description.p: If MaxPacketLifeTime is set, a message that has not been delivered within this time of being queued is abandoned rather than retransmitted. It is -1 if no lifetime limit applies. It cannot be set in conjunction with MaxRetransmits.

field.name: MaxRetransmits
field.comment: The maximum number of times an outgoing message is retransmitted.

description.p: If MaxRetransmits is set, a message that is not delivered after this many retransmissions is abandoned. A value of zero means that each message is sent only once. It is -1 if no retransmission limit applies. It cannot be set in conjunction with MaxPacketLifeTime.

field.name: Negotiated
field.comment: True if the channel was negotiated by the client rather than announced in-band.

description.p: A negotiated channel is created by both peers with the same StreamID, and the remote peer is not notified of its creation. Channels that are announced in-band are delivered to the remote peer through PeerConnection.OnWebChannel.

field.name: OnBufferedAmountLow
field.comment: A callback that is notified when the send queue falls to BufferedAmountLowThreshold.

description.p: The function referenced here is called when BufferedAmount falls from above BufferedAmountLowThreshold to a value at or below it. It is typically used to resume sending after the queue has filled. The callback is only made while the channel is open. The C++ prototype is Function(*WebChannel, APTR Meta).
The Tiri prototype is function(WebChannel).
The callback can send further messages. If these cause the threshold to be crossed again, the next notification is made in a later cycle rather than from within the current callback.

field.name: OnClose
field.comment: A callback that is notified when the channel has closed.

description.p: The function referenced here is called once when the channel closes, whether it was closed by either peer or failed. State is CLOSED when the callback is made. It is not called if the channel is freed. The C++ prototype is Function(*WebChannel, APTR Meta).
The Tiri prototype is function(WebChannel).

field.name: OnError
field.comment: A callback that is notified when the channel fails.

description.p: The function referenced here is called once if the channel fails, and is followed by a call to OnClose. State and Error are updated before the callback is made. The C++ prototype is Function(*WebChannel, ERR Error, APTR Meta).
The Tiri prototype is function(WebChannel, Error).

field.name: OnMessage
field.comment: A callback that receives each message from the remote peer.

description.p: The function referenced here is called for each complete message that is received while the channel is open. The Type is TEXT or BINARY, as declared by the sender. Empty messages are delivered with a length of zero. The C++ prototype is ERR Function(*WebChannel, const void *Data, INT Length, WCM Type, APTR Meta).
The Tiri prototype is function(WebChannel, Buffer, Type), where Buffer is an array<byte>.
The message data is only valid for the duration of the callback, and must be copied if it is to be retained. Errors returned by the callback are logged and otherwise ignored.

field.name: OnOpen
field.comment: A callback that is notified when the channel is ready for use.

description.p: The function referenced here is called once when State changes to OPEN. Messages can be sent with Send from this point. The C++ prototype is Function(*WebChannel, APTR Meta).
The Tiri prototype is function(WebChannel).

field.name: Ordered
field.comment: True if messages are delivered in the order that they were sent.

description.p: If Ordered is false, messages may be delivered to the remote peer in a different order to that in which they were sent.

field.name: Protocol
field.comment: The name of the sub-protocol used by the channel.

description.p: Protocol is a UTF-8 string that is set when the channel is created. It is not interpreted by the channel and is available for the client to identify the format of the messages. It may be empty.

field.name: State
field.comment: The current state of the channel.

description.p: The channel starts in the CONNECTING state and changes to OPEN when OnOpen is called. It changes to CLOSING when either peer starts to close it, and to CLOSED when the closure is complete or the channel fails.
The stream ID identifies the channel on the connection. If the ID was not specified when the channel was created, it is -1 until it is assigned automatically after the DTLS handshake.
